task.description: RE-VALIDATION triggered by a Step 4 (TEST-RUNNER) FAIL against a REAL Keycloak run (not a prior Step 3b FAIL): AC2's tampered-token test asserted exact map equality (`Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body) == %{"error" => "unauthorized"}`) on the rejection response body, but lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex's reject/4 always includes a "detail" key alongside "error" -- a genuine test-assertion bug, not an application regression, but one that made the real-Keycloak run fail: `left: %{"detail" => ..., "error" => "unauthorized"}, right: %{"error" => "unauthorized"}`. TEST-DESIGNER's claimed fix (commits 65f5ced, 4b7a5c5): change AC2's assertion to a partial pattern match, `assert %{"error" => "unauthorized"} = Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body)`, mirroring test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:196's own established pattern. Independently verify: (a) the new assertion is a genuine Elixir pattern match, not something that silently degenerates back to equality; (b) it is equally rigorous to the mirrored line -- still proves rejection actually happened, not merely that some response came back; (c) re-run the real suite against live Keycloak myself and quote real output; (d) test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC2 section matches the fix; (e) full re-check of the other Step 3b criteria against the new commits (no new secrets/TODOs, all 6 ACs still covered).
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
Checked out feature/WF02-REQ134-20260823, git pull confirmed already up to date at commits 65f5ced + 4b7a5c5. Read test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs and test/specs/REQ-134.md fresh from disk (not trusting the resubmission narrative).

(1) AC2 assertion syntax, verified by direct reading (test file line 254): `assert %{"error" => "unauthorized"} = Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body)`. This is a genuine Elixir pattern match, not equality: the right-hand side of `=` is evaluated once, then matched against the map pattern on the left. Elixir map-pattern semantics are explicit here -- a map pattern is a subset match, not a shape match: `%{"error" => "unauthorized"} = %{"error" => "unauthorized", "detail" => "..."}` succeeds because every key named in the pattern ("error") is present in the right-hand map with the exact matching value, and any additional keys the map carries ("detail") are simply ignored by the pattern -- this is standard, well-defined Elixir/Erlang map-matching behavior, not an edge case. `assert <pattern> = <expr>` is ExUnit's documented idiom for this exact kind of match assertion (it raises ExUnit.AssertionError with a match-failure message if the pattern does not match, exactly as `assert x == y` does for equality) -- confirmed this is the identical form already used and passing at test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:196, so the syntax is proven, not merely plausible.

(2) Equivalence to the mirrored line at test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:196 (in the describe block 'missing/malformed token rejected before any DB/JIT work', lines 189-197): identical pattern, identical right-hand-side shape (`Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body)`). Neither assertion is weakened relative to what it needs to prove: in both files, the map-pattern assertion is paired with `assert conn.halted` and `assert conn.status == 401` on the surrounding lines (keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs:248-249; auth_pipeline_test.exs:194-195) -- so 'was this request actually rejected' is established by the halted/status checks, and the body-pattern match's job is narrowly to confirm the JSON error code, which it still does precisely (`"error" => "unauthorized"` must be present with that exact value; a bug that changed the error code, or omitted the key, or returned non-JSON, would still fail this line). Cross-checked reject/4's actual call sites in lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex (lines 151-178): every 401 rejection path calls `reject(conn, 401, "unauthorized", <detail>)`, and reject/4 (line 322) is the sole producer of both keys -- confirmed by reading the function -- so "detail" is unconditionally present on every real 401 response this test could observe, meaning the previous exact-equality assertion was structurally incapable of ever passing against the real verifier, and this fix is the correct one (not a rigor-losing workaround).

(3) Re-ran the real suite myself against the live Keycloak in this environment. `docker compose ps` shows `letflow-keycloak-1` Up (healthy) on host port 8093 (confirmed via .env's LETFLOW_KEYCLOAK_PORT=8093, matching config/keycloak_port.exs's precedence). Ran `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` TWICE consecutively myself (not reusing TEST-DESIGNER's reported numbers): run 1 -> 'Finished in 0.9 seconds ... Result: 3 passed'; run 2 -> 'Finished in 0.8 seconds ... Result: 3 passed'. Both runs green, confirming both the AC2 fix and AC3's reset-then-baseline mechanism (from the prior gate iteration) are genuinely repeatable across invocations against this persistent database, not merely claimed.

(4) test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC2 section (lines 69-95) accurately describes the current fix: states the assertion is now a partial pattern (not exact key-set equality), names the mirrored line in auth_pipeline_test.exs, explains why reject/4 always carries "detail", and records the correction as a Step 4/TEST-RUNNER-triggered fix with the date and the fact that it was a test-assertion bug, not an application regression. Matches the code exactly, no stale narrative.

(5) Re-checked remaining Step 3b criteria against the new diff (git diff ef15ecc..4b7a5c5, the full range covering both the already-PASSED AC3 rework and this round's AC2 fix): no new hardcoded secrets (grepped 'password|secret' across the touched files -- only the same two already-vetted seeded dev credentials, admin-user/admin-pass and designer-user/designer-pass, both pre-existing and unrelated to this diff); no 'TODO: implement test' anywhere; no `@tag :skip` anywhere (grep hits are all prose describing the documented setup_all raise-vs-skip deviation, not an actual skip tag). All 6 ACs still map to runnable tests/mechanisms: AC1 (lines 211-229), AC2 (235-256, this round's fix), AC3 (262-303, reset-then-baseline from the prior PASS, re-confirmed still correct and unchanged in this diff beyond the AC2-adjacent lines), AC4 (test/test_helper.exs exclude mechanism, unchanged), AC5 (setup_all raise, unchanged), AC6 (moduledoc command, unchanged). Fixtures remain isolated (admin-user for AC1/AC2, designer-user for AC3, no collision) and self-sufficient (no test depends on another having run first). No files touched outside the diff scope; no leftover probe files -- this was a read-and-independently-rerun verification, not a mutant-application case (the code under test already existed before this fix; the defect was a test-assertion bug against real, pre-existing application behavior, not a missing module).
